requests.title: AI-assisted clothing and accessories design: voice and hands-on design, sunglasses, full wardrobes, costing, store and marketing
requests.ask: AI agent assisted, software assisted clothing design, where the software handles basically everything including marketing, distribution, manufacturing and manufacturer deals. The designer works in a web browser (and later VR) by voice and by pointing and clicking: describe the garment, get a rendering, give spoken or manual feedback, compare versions. Fabric choices come from what manufacturers offer, with prices, so the designer knows what each shirt costs. From an interview with a designer planning a unisex line with raised, '3D' prints of classical and devotional paintings, sold in Europe and the US, possibly with other brands on the same site for a commission. A second interview added: sunglasses with the brand's logo on the frame and case, starting from a stock frame a manufacturer makes, with the measurements chosen (they estimated about 20 euros to make and 60 to 70 to sell); full-wardrobe sets, started small and limited, with pricing tiers that change fabric quality, and fitted to the target audience (age band, gender, style, climate, season); pieces both in-house and from other brands; and trying garments on virtually, by AI or AR.
requests.next: Live: the studio (voice/typed and drag design, three alternatives, costing, tech pack, quote request, launch kit), a sunglasses designer (stock frame, size, logos, case, cost, quote request with the EU/US test reports) and a wardrobe planner (capsule for an audience, outfit count, in-house vs partner pieces, first drop within a budget). Unproven: whether the designer gets a real garment or pair quoted with it. Next: their artwork and real quotes through it; a printable colour separation from an uploaded painting; then 3D, VR and try-on (ROADMAP.md).
